lecture: Clinical Skills Session 1: Pelvic, Breast, Diabetic Foot & Thyroid Exams

questions.question: A 26-year-old woman is about to have her first pelvic examination for cervical cancer screening. She is fidgeting, breathing quickly, and avoiding eye contact. The clinician sits at eye level and explains what the examination involves. Which statement is most appropriate before beginning?

answers.A: “Do you have any questions or concerns we can discuss before we begin?”
answers.B: “I will be quick, so there is no need to go through each step.”
answers.C: “Just try to relax, and this will be over before you know it.”
answers.D: “Lie back on the bed and scoot down toward the end for me.”
answers.E: “There is nothing to be nervous about, since everyone has this done.”

explanations.A: A trauma-informed approach identifies concerns and asks about comfort before the examination, which helps restore a sense of safety and autonomy.
explanations.B: Efficiency matters, but each component should be introduced and explained, with permission asked.
explanations.C: Telling an anxious patient to relax dismisses her cues and offers no control over what happens.
explanations.D: The phrase for me and the word bed carry unintended connotations; exam table and neutral instructions are preferred.
explanations.E: Explaining that the exam is standard is helpful, but minimizing her feelings is not.

questions.question: A clinician completes a breast and pelvic examination on a 31-year-old woman, and all findings are normal. Which statement is the most appropriate way to share the results?

answers.C: “Thank you for holding so still for me.”
answers.D: “You look perfect, with nothing to worry about.”

explanations.A: Results should be given in simple, clinical language; this phrasing is recommended over comments that could be heard as evaluating her body.
explanations.B: Looks great can be taken as a personal comment, and down there is vague, non-clinical language.
explanations.C: The phrase for me should be avoided, and this does not communicate the findings.
explanations.D: Describing the patient's body as perfect is not professional clinical language.
explanations.E: Words such as beautiful are inappropriate when describing a sensitive examination.

questions.question: A 34-year-old woman is scheduled for a pelvic examination. She says she would feel most comfortable if her sister, who accompanied her to the visit, served as the chaperone. Which is the most appropriate response?

answers.A: Allow her sister to serve as the only chaperone for the examination
answers.B: Ask her sister to step out and proceed without any chaperone present
answers.C: Have a medical staff member chaperone and let her sister stay in the room
answers.D: Have a medical staff member chaperone and require her sister to leave
answers.E: Postpone the examination until she is able to come to a visit alone

explanations.A: A family member generally should not serve as the chaperone.
explanations.B: A chaperone should be present for a pelvic examination.
explanations.C: The chaperone should be a member of the medical staff, but a family member or friend may remain in the room if the patient prefers.
explanations.D: The patient's preferred support person may remain in addition to the staff chaperone.
explanations.E: There is no reason to delay care; her preference can be accommodated alongside a staff chaperone.

questions.question: A 41-year-old woman with spastic cerebral palsy is due for cervical cancer screening. She uses a wheelchair and says she was unable to place her feet in the footrests at a previous attempt. Which is the most appropriate first step?

answers.A: Arrange the examination under general anesthesia
answers.B: Ask her which position works best for her body
answers.D: Have two assistants hold her legs in the footrests
answers.E: Place her knee-to-chest, which suits most patients

explanations.A: Anesthesia is considered only when no alternative positioning can be tolerated.
explanations.B: The clinician should begin by asking what works best for the patient; alternatives to lithotomy such as the diamond, V, M, or knee-to-chest positions are offered if she is unsure.
explanations.C: Mobility impairment is not a reason to withhold recommended screening.
explanations.D: Forcing the standard position ignores her experience and may cause pain or injury.
explanations.E: No single alternative suits everyone; the choice should start with the patient's own preference.

questions.question: A 62-year-old woman has 8 months of vulvar itching and pain with intercourse. Examination shows thin white patches with loss of pigment and hair, fissures at the interlabial folds, fusion of the labia minora with the labia majora, and a clitoris buried beneath a fused prepuce. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

explanations.A: Low-estrogen atrophy causes dryness, sparse hair, and reduced turgor but not white patches with burying of the clitoris.
explanations.B: Candidiasis causes itching with a thick white cottage cheese-like discharge and no architectural change.
explanations.C: Genital warts are fleshy, exophytic, warty lesions rather than atrophic white patches.
explanations.D: Genital herpes presents with painful clusters of vesicles.
explanations.E: Lichen sclerosus presents with pruritus, pain, and dyspareunia, with white fragile patches, fissures, and loss of normal vulvar architecture including burying of the clitoris.

questions.question: A 57-year-old woman whose last menstrual period was 5 years ago reports vaginal dryness and pain with intercourse. Examination shows scarce pubic hair, decreased turgor of the vulvar skin, and decreased moisture at the introitus. There are no white patches or vesicles. Which is the underlying cause?

explanations.A: Androgen excess causes hirsutism, acne, and clitoromegaly rather than atrophy.
explanations.B: Hypercortisolism causes skin thinning and striae but is not the cause of postmenopausal vulvovaginal atrophy.
explanations.C: Atrophic vaginitis, or genitourinary syndrome of menopause, results from a decreased-estrogen state and can occur at any age when estrogen is low.
explanations.D: Vulvovaginal epithelial thickness and moisture depend on estrogen rather than progesterone.
explanations.E: Hypothyroidism causes doughy skin, hair loss, and cold intolerance, not isolated vulvovaginal atrophy.

questions.question: A 28-year-old woman reports a malodorous vaginal discharge without itching or pain. Speculum examination shows a thin, whitish-gray discharge coating the vaginal walls. Wet mount shows epithelial cells whose borders are obscured by adherent bacteria. Overgrowth of which organism is responsible?

explanations.A: Candida causes a thick white cottage cheese-like discharge with branching hyphae on potassium hydroxide preparation.
explanations.B: Chlamydia causes cervicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease and does not produce clue cells.
explanations.C: Bacterial vaginosis is due to overgrowth of Gardnerella and produces a thin, gray, malodorous discharge with clue cells on wet mount.
explanations.D: Genital herpes presents with painful clustered vesicles rather than discharge.
explanations.E: Trichomoniasis causes a frothy discharge with cervical petechiae and motile protozoa on wet mount.

questions.question: A 17-year-old girl who takes a combined estrogen-progestin contraceptive has a speculum examination. A symmetric, red, velvety area surrounds the cervical os. She has no symptoms, there is no discharge, and cervical cytology is normal. Which explanation is most likely?

answers.A: Dysplasia of squamous epithelium within the transformation zone
answers.B: Eversion of endocervical columnar epithelium onto the ectocervix
answers.C: Punctate hemorrhages of the ectocervix from protozoal infection
answers.D: Thinning of ectocervical squamous epithelium from low estrogen
answers.E: Ulceration of ectocervical epithelium from herpes simplex virus

explanations.A: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia has irregular borders, atypical vessels, and acetowhite change, with abnormal cytology.
explanations.B: Ectropion is a normal variant in which columnar epithelium is exposed to the vagina; it is common in adolescents, pregnancy, and estrogen-progestin contraceptive use.
explanations.C: Trichomoniasis causes cervical petechiae together with a frothy discharge.
explanations.D: Atrophy occurs in low-estrogen states, not in an adolescent taking exogenous estrogen.
explanations.E: Herpetic lesions are painful vesicles or ulcers, not a painless symmetric velvety area.

questions.question: A 33-year-old woman who tests positive for high-risk human papillomavirus undergoes colposcopy. After application of acetic acid, a lesion with an irregular border and atypical blood vessels turns white. This type of lesion most commonly arises in which location?

answers.A: Internal os of the cervical canal
answers.B: Lower segment of the uterine cavity

explanations.A: Lesions arise at the squamocolumnar junction near the external os rather than at the internal os.
explanations.B: The endometrial lining cannot be seen on speculum examination and is not where these lesions originate.
explanations.C: The posterior fornix is the deepest recess of vaginal tissue around the cervix and is not the usual site of cervical neoplasia.
explanations.D: The transformation zone, between the squamous ectocervix and the columnar endocervix, is a common site of cervical cancer and its precursor lesions.
explanations.E: The vestibule contains the urethral meatus and vaginal introitus and is not the site of cervical neoplasia.

questions.question: During a routine bimanual examination of a 30-year-old woman, the examiner feels the cervix but cannot palpate the uterine fundus between the internal and external hands. She has no symptoms and a negative pregnancy test. Ultrasonography later shows a normal uterus tilted toward the sacrum. Which examination technique allows palpation of her uterus?

explanations.A: The inguinal nodes do not provide information about uterine position or size.
explanations.B: Moving the fingers to the lateral fornices is used to examine the ovaries and adnexa.
explanations.C: A retroflexed, retroverted uterus is a normal variant that is not easily felt on bimanual examination and requires a rectovaginal examination.
explanations.D: The speculum allows inspection of only the vagina and cervix, not palpation of the uterine body.
explanations.E: A posteriorly tilted fundus lies away from the anterior abdominal wall and cannot be felt from above.

questions.question: A 42-year-old woman has had increasingly heavy and painful menstrual periods for 2 years. Her hemoglobin is 9.8 g/dL. On bimanual examination the uterus is enlarged and irregular, with several rubbery, non-tender nodules. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

explanations.A: Atrophy causes dryness and dyspareunia in low-estrogen states, not heavy menses with a nodular uterus.
explanations.B: This is an asymptomatic cervical lesion seen on colposcopy and does not enlarge the uterus.
explanations.C: An ovarian cyst is a solitary smooth, round, mobile mass in the adnexa rather than in the uterus.
explanations.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease presents with fever, discharge, and cervical and adnexal tenderness.
explanations.E: Fibroids may be asymptomatic or cause dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia, and they are felt as one or more rubbery, non-tender nodules or masses.

questions.question: A 22-year-old woman has 4 days of lower abdominal pain, fever, and vaginal discharge. Her temperature is 38.6°C. On examination there is purulent discharge at the cervical os, marked tenderness when the cervix is palpated, and tenderness of both adnexa without a discrete mass. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

explanations.A: Bacterial vaginosis causes a malodorous thin discharge without fever or pelvic tenderness.
explanations.B: Ectropion is an asymptomatic normal variant with no tenderness or fever.
explanations.C: An ovarian cyst is a smooth, mobile adnexal mass that may cause pain but not fever and discharge.
explanations.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease typically presents with vaginal discharge, fever, and pelvic pain, with tenderness on palpation of the cervix and of one or both adnexa.
explanations.E: Fibroids are rubbery, non-tender nodules associated with heavy, painful periods.

questions.question: A 28-year-old woman reports 6 months of a deepening voice, worsening acne, and irregular menstrual periods. Examination shows coarse hair on the chin and chest, pubic hair in a diamond-shaped distribution, and an enlarged clitoris. These findings indicate an excess of which class of hormone?

explanations.A: Signs of androgen excess include hirsutism with a diamond-shaped pubic hair pattern, acne, male-pattern balding, voice deepening, clitoromegaly, and menstrual irregularity.
explanations.B: Estrogen excess does not cause virilization; estrogen supports the normal triangular female pubic hair pattern.
explanations.C: Mineralocorticoid excess causes hypertension and hypokalemia rather than virilization.
explanations.D: Progestins do not produce clitoromegaly or deepening of the voice.
explanations.E: Thyroid hormone excess causes weight loss, tremor, and heat intolerance, not hirsutism.

questions.question: A 13-year-old girl is seen for a well visit. Her pubic hair is coarse and curly and covers the entire mons pubis but does not extend onto the medial thighs. The areolae are elevated above the contour of the breasts. Which sexual maturity rating best describes her development?

explanations.A: Stage 1 is preadolescent, with no pubic hair and no breast development.
explanations.B: Stage 2 is long, straight, downy hair along the labia with elevation of the breast and areola.
explanations.C: Stage 3 is darker, coarser hair spreading sparsely over the mons with enlargement of the breast and areola.
explanations.D: Stage 4 is coarse curly hair over the entire mons pubis without spread to the thighs, with the areola elevated above the breast.
explanations.E: Stage 5 hair extends to the proximal medial thighs, and the areola returns to the contour of the breast.

questions.question: A 58-year-old woman notices a lump in her left breast. Examination shows a 3-cm firm, fixed, non-tender mass in the upper outer quadrant. The overlying skin has a stippled pattern resembling the rind of an orange, and a firm left axillary lymph node is palpable. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

explanations.A: A fibroadenoma is a rubbery, well-circumscribed, freely mobile mass, typically in younger women.
explanations.B: An abscess is a tender, warm, fluctuant mass, often with fever.
explanations.C: Breast cancer typically presents as a firm, fixed, non-tender mass; peau d'orange and lymphadenopathy indicate underlying carcinoma.
explanations.D: Fibrocystic changes are usually bilateral, tender, and variable with the menstrual cycle.
explanations.E: A simple cyst is smooth, round, and mobile and does not alter the overlying skin.

questions.question: A 58-year-old man with a 20-year history of type 2 diabetes has had a red, hot, swollen left foot for 3 weeks with surprisingly little pain. He is afebrile and has no break in the skin. The arch of the midfoot has collapsed, and he cannot feel a 10-g monofilament on either foot. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

explanations.A: Charcot arthropathy occurs in the neuropathic foot, most often in the midfoot, and may present as a unilateral red, hot, swollen, flat foot with marked deformity.
explanations.B: Claw toe is hyperextension at the metatarsophalangeal joint with interphalangeal flexion that raises plantar pressure.
explanations.C: A bunion is a forefoot deformity that can cause pressure ulcers between the toes but not collapse of the midfoot.
explanations.D: Hammer toe is a deformity of a toe joint, often from ill-fitting shoes, and does not cause a hot, swollen midfoot.
explanations.E: Tinea pedis causes scaling and skin breakdown, especially between the toes, without joint collapse.

questions.question: A 63-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has a foot examination. A 10-g nylon monofilament is applied to the first, third, and fifth metatarsal heads and to the plantar surface of the distal hallux, avoiding areas of callus. She cannot feel it at any site on the right foot. Which does this finding most directly indicate?

answers.A: Loss of arterial perfusion from peripheral vascular disease
answers.B: Loss of joint stability from neuropathic midfoot collapse
answers.C: Loss of protective sensation from large-fiber nerve dysfunction
answers.D: Loss of skin integrity from a fungal infection of the foot
answers.E: Loss of the Achilles reflex from a lumbar nerve root lesion

explanations.A: Perfusion is assessed by palpating the dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses and by the ankle-brachial index.
explanations.B: Charcot arthropathy is recognized on inspection as a deformed, swollen midfoot.
explanations.C: Inability to sense the 10-g monofilament reflects loss of large-fiber nerve function and identifies loss of protective sensation, a pathway to foot ulceration.
explanations.D: Tinea pedis is identified by inspection for scaling and breakdown, not by monofilament testing.
explanations.E: The ankle reflex is tested separately with a reflex hammer and assesses a different pathway.

questions.question: A 66-year-old man with type 2 diabetes who smokes reports cramping calf pain when walking two blocks that is relieved by rest. His feet are cool, and neither the dorsalis pedis nor the posterior tibial pulse can be palpated on either side. Which is the most appropriate next test?

explanations.A: The monofilament test assesses protective sensation, not arterial supply.
explanations.B: The tuning fork assesses vibration sense as part of the neurologic examination.
explanations.C: The ankle reflex evaluates neuropathy and does not assess perfusion.
explanations.D: A patient with abnormal pedal pulses should have an ankle-brachial index; a value below 0.8 is associated with claudication and below 0.4 with rest pain and tissue necrosis.
explanations.E: A skin scraping evaluates suspected tinea pedis and would not explain claudication with absent pulses.

questions.question: A 44-year-old woman has perioral tingling and painful hand cramps 2 days after total thyroidectomy. When a blood pressure cuff is inflated above her systolic pressure for 3 minutes, her hand goes into spasm. Tapping in front of the tragus causes twitching around the mouth. Laboratory results are shown. Which is the cause of her findings?

answers.A: Decreased PTH secretion after injury to the parathyroid glands
answers.B: Decreased thyroid hormone after removal of the thyroid gland
answers.C: Deficiency of vitamin D from poor intestinal absorption
answers.D: Resistance of kidney and bone to the actions of PTH
answers.E: Suppressed PTH secretion in response to high serum calcium

explanations.A: The most common cause of primary hypoparathyroidism is iatrogenic, from thyroidectomy; the resulting hypocalcemia produces Trousseau and Chvostek signs.
explanations.B: Hypothyroidism develops over weeks and causes bradycardia and delayed reflex relaxation, not tetany.
explanations.C: Vitamin D deficiency lowers calcium and phosphorus and raises PTH.
explanations.D: End-organ resistance would produce hypocalcemia with an elevated PTH.
explanations.E: This describes secondary hypoparathyroidism, but her calcium is low rather than high.

questions.question: A 31-year-old woman has lost 6 kg over 3 months and reports heat intolerance and a tremor. Her pulse is 112/min. Examination shows lid lag, protrusion of both eyes, a diffusely enlarged thyroid with an audible bruit, brisk reflexes, and a raised rash over both shins. Laboratory results are shown. Which mechanism underlies her disease?

answers.A: Adenoma of the pituitary that secretes thyrotropin
answers.B: Antibodies that block the thyrotropin receptor
answers.C: Antibodies that destroy thyroid follicular cells
answers.D: Antibodies that stimulate the thyrotropin receptor
answers.E: Deficiency of iodine in the thyroid follicles

explanations.A: A TSH-secreting adenoma would give an elevated or inappropriately normal TSH rather than a suppressed one.
explanations.B: Blocking antibodies would reduce hormone synthesis and cause hypothyroidism.
explanations.C: Destructive autoimmunity causes hypothyroidism with bradycardia, doughy skin, and delayed reflex relaxation.
explanations.D: Graves disease is an autoimmune condition in which antibodies to the thyrotropin receptor stimulate hormone synthesis; it may be associated with exophthalmos and pretibial myxedema.
explanations.E: Iodine deficiency causes goiter with a normal or elevated TSH and does not cause eye or skin findings.
